subject: Per-token ladder, pilot credits & sustainability buffer
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@healthspark.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing options for per-token ladder + pilot credits

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the demo last week. HealthSpark is planning to ramp a consumer-facing feature that will call your hosted API for chat+summaries. We expect a quick ramp: roughly 8B tokens next quarter, growing to ~30–50B tokens/quarter within 12 months depending on adoption.

Two asks as we evaluate Redwood: 1) a per-token ladder with clear breakpoints and whether you price on a marginal basis (each token priced at the bracket it falls into) vs a blended effective rate; 2) whether you can support a short pilot with credits (we'd like something that covers early production variability).

A third consideration for us: seasonality / product toggles could cause usage drops. We'd like some kind of "sustainability buffer" or carryover so we don't get penalized for conservative forecasting in month one after a product change. Is that something Redwood has been willing to offer (e.g., small percentage carryover or one-time pause of a fraction of committed tokens)?

I've attached a high-level usage forecast (HS_usage_forecast_Q3-Q4.xlsx) and can share more detail if helpful. Looking for a quick sketch of options so we can discuss with finance this week.

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Platform Partnerships
HealthSpark

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@healthspark.ai>
Cc: Rahul Desai <rahul.desai@healthspark.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing options for per-token ladder + pilot credits

Samantha —

Thanks for the clear forecast and the call earlier. High-level options we can put on the table quickly: 

- Hybrid ladder (recommended): marginal rates at breakpoints (so each additional token steps to the next rate) with a blended floor calculation applied at quarterly true-up if you prefer a single effective rate for accounting.
- Commit tiers (example breakpoints): 1B / 5B / 20B tokens per quarter. We can show modeled unit economics across those bands.
- Pilot accelerator: we can provide starter credits to remove early friction. I can commit to a pilot credit of 250k tokens up front; open to increasing subject to internal approval.
- Sustainability buffer: we have a concept for a short carryover (~10% of committed volume) that can be applied one quarter forward or used against overage; requires legal language but we can include a one-time buffer for early-stage ramps.
- True-up cadence: quarterly true-ups are standard; we can also do monthly reporting for visibility.

I've attached a concise summary (redwood-pricing-summary-v3.pdf) with example math for marginal vs blended scenarios. Want to hop on a 30-min call to walk through the numbers with finance and show cost sensitivity to breakpoints?

Thanks —
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Lee <samantha@healthspark.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 08:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing options for per-token ladder + pilot credits

Alex —

That all sounds reasonable. A few clarifying questions before we schedule a finance call: 

1) How do you apply pilot/accelerator credits? Against committed volume, or only to overage in the pilot period? We prefer credits to reduce our committed invoice in a pilot.
2) If you do both marginal pricing and offer a blended floor at true-up, how is the blended rate computed? (weighted average across brackets or capped at the lowest marginal bracket?)
3) Do embeddings and chat tokens fall under the same ladder/rates or are they separate SKUs?
4) For the sustainability buffer: can that be used one-time only, and is there a lookback period for seasonality justification?

I'm looping Rahul (finance) on this thread. I've re-attached the forecast so you can see monthly granularity.

—Samantha

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha@healthspark.ai>, Rahul Desai <rahul.desai@healthspark.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Pricing options for per-token ladder + pilot credits — internal: margin/credit ask

Team —

FYI: HealthSpark is evaluating a ladder and asked about pilot credits + a one-time "sustainability buffer" (~10% carryover). They're early but forecast 8B next quarter -> 30–50B within 12 months. I proposed a 250k token accelerator but we may need to increase to land the commit.

Quick asks: 
- Can we approve up to 300k in accelerator credits to be applied against their first quarter committed invoice?
- Are we comfortable with a one-time 10% sustainability buffer that can be carried forward one quarter (requires legal visibility but should be ok for smaller strategic pilots)?
- If we go hybrid (marginal + blended true-up), how do we model the worst-case revenue impact — Karthik, can you run a sensitivity with their attached forecast?

Attachments: HS_usage_forecast_Q3-Q4.xlsx

Thanks,
Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 14:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Pricing options for per-token ladder + pilot credits — internal: margin/credit ask

Alex / Karthik —

We can approve accelerator credits up to 300k tokens for this pilot and roll that against their first-quarter committed invoice. Finance wants blended vs marginal sensitivity; please run both:

- Marginal: standard step pricing at breakpoints.
- Blended floor: weighted average across actual usage at quarter true-up (so they get the benefit of lower brackets if volume pushes there).

We are ok to pilot a one-time 10% sustainability buffer (carryover for one quarter only) but legal must add explicit language: buffer is non-recurring, cannot be stacked across quarters, and any excess carryover beyond buffer is subject to standard clawback. Cap exposure to a fixed dollar threshold tied to the accelerator budget.

Karthik — please run the sensitivity by EOD PST and flag any downside scenarios where our blended reconciliation would create >20% margin erosion vs base case.

Marissa
VP, Revenue Operations

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@healthspark.ai>, Rahul Desai <rahul.desai@healthspark.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing options for per-token ladder + pilot credits

Samantha / Rahul —

Thanks for the patience while we pulled internal approvals. Summarizing the proposal that Marissa and Finance have greenlit for your pilot: 

1) Pilot accelerator: 300k tokens applied against HealthSpark's first-quarter committed invoice (can be used for committed volume or overage in Q1).
2) Proposed commit breakpoints (quarterly): 1B / 5B / 20B tokens. Pricing will be on a marginal basis during the quarter; at quarterly true-up we can compute a blended effective rate if you request it (blended = usage-weighted average across the marginal brackets for that quarter).
3) True-up cadence: quarterly (reporting monthly). Invoices subject to 60-day terms per usual.
4) Sustainability buffer: one-time 10% carryover of committed volume to the following quarter. Buffer is non-recurring and limited to one quarter; any amount beyond the buffer will follow standard true-up/clawback mechanics. Legal will add precise language to the SOW.
4) SKUs: chat and embeddings will share the same per-token ladder for this agreement (we'll include a line item to clarify token type mapping in the SOW).

Next steps: I'll have legal/solutions send a proposed SOW and the DocuSign link. If the above aligns, please confirm and share the PO contact for invoicing. Attaching the pricing summary and proposed SOW draft for your records.

Link to SOW (DocuSign): https://redwood.app/docusign/HS-4721-SOW

Appreciate the partnership — looking forward to getting you running.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
